description: Generate the canonical single round-robin opponent table by the circle method.

source.discovery_scope: Pinned popular-title metadata only; no Rosetta task wording, examples, tests, implementations, or code used.
source.algorithm_description: Ribeiro et al., A tutorial on graph models for scheduling round-robin sports tournaments, Algorithm 1 (circle method), DOI 10.1111/itor.13290.
source.independent_description: The same circle construction is independently described as the clock method by Boschetti and Righini, Teaching Integer Programming by Scheduling the Belgian Soccer League, DOI 10.1287/ited.2022.0269.

input.extra_word_behavior: Reject a two-word parseable frame as malformed.
input.validation_order: Validate non-null pointer, array length, and team-count domain before output pointer or capacity checks.

output.encoding: [team_count,round_count,opponent_table...], unsigned bytes; rows are team IDs in ascending order, columns are rounds in ascending order, and 0xff denotes a bye.
output.odd_team_rule: Pad to the next even team count with a dummy pivot; omit dummy games so one real team has opponent 0xff per round.

workspace.accounting: Fixed opponent table of at most 8*7 bytes, padded ring of at most 7 team IDs, and scalar loop state; caller input/output buffers excluded.

complexity.primary: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) workspace for modular pair generation and the opponent table.
complexity.independent: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) workspace for the rotating-ring construction and opponent table.
